bibliographic.title: Assessing the User Experience of an LLM-Based Conversational Assistant in Diabetes Mellitus Care
bibliographic.authors: Vasco Furtado, Jorge Araujo, Elizabeth S. Furtado, Rafael Bomfim, Vitória Silva, Nickolas Mororó, Lucas Vasconcelos, Cecília Carvalho, Marcos Severo, Juliana Torres, Juliana Oliveira, Antonio Bruno Freitas
bibliographic.citation_apa: Furtado, V., Araujo, J., Furtado, E. S., Bomfim, R., Silva, V., Mororó, N., Vasconcelos, L., Carvalho, C., Severo, M., Torres, J., Oliveira, J., & Freitas, A. B. (2025). Assessing the user experience of an LLM-based conversational assistant in diabetes mellitus care. Journal of Healthcare Informatics Research, 10, 116–153. https://doi.org/10.1007/s41666-025-00217-5

methodology.study_design: 3-month longitudinal study comparing personalized vs non-personalized LLM assistant interactions
methodology.sample_description: Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus using MarIA via a messaging platform
methodology.technology_context: GPT-3.5-powered virtual assistant (MarIA) with multi-agent architecture, prompt engineering, and messaging-platform delivery for diabetes self-care

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article empirically evaluates a GPT-3.5 multi-agent conversational assistant in diabetes care and reports engagement outcomes plus safety concerns, making it relevant to conversational AI in regulated healthcare. However, the primary contribution in the provided text is UX, personalization, and engagement rather than a governance, accountability, compliance, or oversight framework, so it is better classified as supporting evidence than central governance evidence.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial excerpts were provided; full methods, ethics, governance mechanisms, and limitation sections were not fully visible for complete methodological appraisal.

appraisal.notes: Clear empirical objective and longitudinal design are evident, with quantified engagement findings and explicit safety concerns. Detailed procedures for data collection, ethical approval, statistical analysis, and operational governance controls are not fully available in the supplied excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: Findings on engagement and safety are coherent and relevant to LLM conversational assistants in healthcare, but the supplied text provides limited detail on governance mechanisms, auditability, human oversight, and full analytic methods, reducing confidence for governance-focused synthesis.

coding.theme: User experience and safety of an LLM-based conversational assistant in diabetes care
coding.subtheme: Personalization-driven engagement with safety-layer needs in regulated healthcare
rq_alignment: LLM conversational systems in regulated healthcare
safety and risk control in generative conversational assistants
operational governance through profiling and safety layers

synthesis.main_claim: A GPT-3.5-based multi-agent conversational assistant for type 2 diabetes care increased engagement and message depth through personalization, while safety review showed a need for embedded detection of potentially unsuitable recommendations.
synthesis.contribution: Provides empirical longitudinal evidence on LLM assistant engagement in healthcare and identifies safety-layer requirements tied to patient profiling and recommendation appropriateness.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied text emphasizes UX outcomes and high-level safety concerns; it does not fully document governance processes such as human oversight, audit logs, compliance controls, or post-deployment monitoring frameworks.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting empirical evidence on conversational LLM deployment in regulated healthcare, especially for engagement-personalization tradeoffs and the need for embedded safety controls before or after recommendation delivery.
